expl.summary: Every jet is placed on 16 scales. Each scale is a sum of if-statements on jet observables, clipped at zero. Each class score adds some scales and subtracts others, and the formula's validation accuracy is 65.4%. In this setup MARS was not offered the W, Z, H or top mass values as thresholds. With 8 particles the jet mass is the mass of the 8 hardest particles only, so the mass cuts the formula does use (29.6, 53.3, 60.6, 64.6, 69.6, 76.7 and 88.2 GeV) do not sit at the boson or top masses, and most neurons are built from widths (ΣzΔR, ΣzΔR², λ₁+λ₂, λ₁) rather than from mass. The t score follows jet size: it subtracts the compactness scale (neuron 13, ΣzΔR < 0.148, -47%) and adds the overall-size scale (neuron 10, +26%), so it rises with ΣzΔR, λ₁+λ₂ and Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ (rank correlations 0.92). The q score is mostly the narrow-jet scale (neuron 9, +56%), and it subtracts overall size (neuron 10, -18%). The g score is led by a scale that falls with jet mass and subjet-pair mass (neuron 2, +38%), adds the narrow-jet scale (neuron 9, +22%), and subtracts the scale for pT held in the 3 hardest particles (neuron 5, -14.5%). The W score is led by the compact-centred scale (neuron 11, +24%). The Z score is led by the elongated-jet scale with mass/pT between 0.073 and 0.108 (neuron 7, +35%). Both boson scores subtract the wide-angle-radiation scales (neurons 3 and 6). W and Z are split mainly by two λ₁+λ₂-band scales: neuron 14 (λ₁+λ₂ 0.0036-0.0067, mass/pT above 0.085) enters the Z score with +6% and the W score with -9%, and neuron 15 (λ₁+λ₂ below 0.0132, ΣzΔR above 0.102, small e₂) takes -8% out of the W score and -2% out of the Z score.

0.title: compact jets with subjet axes 0.107-0.301 apart, not the narrowest
0.measures: Pushed up by ΣzΔR² < 0.0132 (+7.9% of its input, its strongest term), λ₁+λ₂ < 0.00868 (+7.3%), 0.107 < max ΔR(3 subjets) < 0.301 (+5.3%, +4.5%) and e₂ < 0.0356 (+3.8%). Pushed down for the very narrowest jets (λ₁+λ₂ < 0.00437, -7.3%; ΣzΔR < 0.0761, -3.5%; λ₁ < 0.00543, -2.6%) and for small mass/pT (< 0.0848, -5.2%). Overall it rises with 1−λ₂/λ₁ (rank correlation 0.555) and falls with planar flow (-0.555), N₂ (-0.545) and τ₂₁ (-0.538). Mean values: W (2.01), Z (1.93), t (0.37), g (0.16), q (0.15). It is non-zero for 76.6% of W and 78.3% of Z jets, but only 14.0% of gluon, 12.6% of quark and 19.9% of top jets.
0.role: It raises the W score (+10%) and lowers the g score (-6%). It does not enter the q, Z or t scores.

1.title: wide jets at high total pT with small mass/pT
1.measures: Pushed down for narrow jets (ΣzΔR² < 0.00868, -10.8%, its strongest term; λ₁+λ₂ < 0.0061, -7.4%; ΣzΔR < 0.102, -6.3%) and when the 5 hardest particles carry more than 531 GeV (-7.9%). Pushed up by (mass/pT)² < 0.00583 (+8.0%), high total pT (log of total pT > 6.50, +6.1%, and > 6.38, +4.1%), ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² < 0.00817 (+4.4%) and z₇ > 0.0232 (+4.4%). It rises with ΣzΔR and Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ (rank correlation 0.617) and λ₁ (0.611). Mean values: t (1.31), Z (0.98), g (0.73), W (0.58), q (0.31). It is zero for 65.3% of quark jets, 51.0% of gluon jets and 13.6% of top jets.
1.role: It raises the g score (+13%) and the Z score (+4%). It does not enter the q, W or t scores.

2.title: light jets: falls with jet mass and largest subjet-pair mass
2.measures: Its largest terms act on the 8th-hardest particle: z₇ > 0.0232 (-11.0%) and pT_7 < 53.4 GeV (-10.5%) push it down, while pT_7 > 20.1 GeV (+6.1%) and pT_7 < 43.5 GeV (+4.1%) push it up. It is also pushed down by Σz(ΔR/0.8)^½ > 0.112 (-7.3%) and by less than 717 GeV in the 5 hardest particles (-6.5%), and pushed up by total pT < 788 GeV (+5.1%), λ₁ < 0.0120 (+4.0%) and largest subjet-pair mass < 63.7 GeV (+3.7%). Overall it falls with the largest subjet-pair mass (rank correlation -0.751) and jet mass (-0.747) and rises with M₂ (0.67). Mean values: g (3.57), q (2.62), W (1.70), Z (1.41), t (1.20). It is non-zero for most jets (96.3% of gluon jets, 82.0% of top jets).
2.role: It raises the g score (+38%), where it is the largest input. It does not enter the q, W, Z or t scores.

3.title: wide jets with pT at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4
3.measures: Its strongest term, ΣzΔR² > 0.00868, pushes it down (-19.4%), but ΣzΔR > 0.0408 (+11.1%), λ₁+λ₂ > 0.00752 (+6.8%), mass/pT > 0.0681 (+6.1%), λ₁ > 0.00838 (+5.8%) and ΣzΔR > 0.0761 (+4.8%) push it up, so only jets that are wide on several measures together end up above zero; τ₁ > 0.0536 pushes it down (-8.2%). It follows the pT share (rank correlation 0.716) and the number of particles (0.706) at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4. Mean values: t (3.41), g (0.84), q (0.43), Z (0.11), W (0.01). It is non-zero for 75.0% of top jets but only 0.5% of W, 15.4% of Z, 18.3% of gluon and 9.1% of quark jets.
3.role: It lowers the W score (-15%) and the Z score (-22%), and raises the t score slightly (+2%). It does not enter the g or q scores.

4.title: small ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² with sizeable mass/pT (low τ₂₁, N₂, D₂)
4.measures: Two terms dominate: ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² < 0.0117 pushes it up (+28.8%) and (mass/pT)² < 0.0117 pushes it down (-23.2%), so it is high when the jet has sizeable mass relative to its pT but a small angular spread ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ². Smaller terms include ΣzᵢzⱼΔRᵢⱼ² < 0.0172 (+4.6%), ΣzΔR² < 0.0188 (-4.6%) and mass < 76.7 GeV (+2.7%). It falls with τ₂₁ (rank correlation -0.618), N₂ (-0.615) and D₂ (-0.606). Mean values: Z (2.26), t (1.50), W (1.41), g (0.54), q (0.31). It is zero for 75.2% of quark and 63.9% of gluon jets and 17.4% of Z jets.
4.role: It raises the Z score (+4%) and the t score (+5%) and lowers the q score (-8%). It does not enter the g or W scores. Freezing it at its mean changes the accuracy by only -0.04 points.

5.title: pT held by the 3 hardest particles, small τ₁ and e₂
5.measures: Pushed up by τ₁ < 0.0954 (+6.7%), log of total pT > 6.27 (+6.4%), ΣzΔR² < 0.00165 with centroid offset < 0.0236 (+4.6%) and ΣzΔR² < 0.00264 (+3.7%); pushed down by mass/pT < 0.0904 (-6.0%) and by the 8th-hardest particle having pT > 23.2 GeV (-5.6%) or < 37.2 GeV (-4.7%). Overall it rises with the summed pT of the 3 hardest (rank correlation 0.71) and 5 hardest particles (0.707) and falls with e₂ (-0.705), τ₁ (-0.695) and z₇ (-0.689). Mean values: q (4.61), g (1.51), W (1.38), Z (1.35), t (0.37). It is non-zero for 89.9% of quark jets and only 35.2% of top jets.
5.role: It raises the q score (+6%) and lowers the g score (-14.5%) and the t score (-16%). It does not enter the W or Z scores.

6.title: wide jets (λ₁+λ₂ above 0.0132) with λ₁ below 0.0120
6.measures: Pushed down for narrow jets (ΣzΔR² < 0.00868, -15.0%, its strongest term; λ₁+λ₂ < 0.0132, -9.9%; max ΔR < 0.145, -4.5%) and pushed up by λ₁ < 0.0120 (+8.7%), max ΔR(3 subjets) < 0.179 (+5.4%), τ₁ < 0.114 (+4.5%) and mass/pT < 0.0904 (+4.0%). It follows the pT share (rank correlation 0.518) and number of particles (0.514) at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4, the centroid offset (0.509) and λ₁+λ₂ (0.482). Mean values: t (2.72), g (1.25), q (0.57), Z (0.35), W (0.08). It is zero for 92.0% of W and 66.1% of Z jets and for 20.9% of top jets.
6.role: It raises the g score (+5%) and the q score (+9%), and lowers the W score (-9%) and the Z score (-15%). It does not enter the t score.

7.title: elongated jets (high 1−λ₂/λ₁, low τ₂₁) with mass/pT from 0.073 to 0.108
7.measures: Built from many small terms on λ₁+λ₂ and mass/pT: it is pushed down for narrow jets (ΣzΔR < 0.0872, -6.6%; λ₁+λ₂ < 0.00668, -6.2%) and for mass/pT above 0.0111 (-6.6%), 0.0904 (-5.7%) and 0.108 (-3.1%), and pushed up by mass/pT above 0.0848 (+3.5%) and 0.0727 (+3.1%), ΣzΔR² > 0.0132 (+4.6%), max ΔR(3 subjets) > 0.143 (+3.6%) and ΔR(2 subjets) < 0.159 (+3.2%). It rises with 1−λ₂/λ₁ (rank correlation 0.559) and falls with planar flow (-0.559), τ₂₁ with β = 2 (-0.484) and D₂ (-0.483). Mean values: Z (3.91), W (2.68), t (1.08), g (1.06), q (0.54). It is non-zero for 92.9% of Z and 91.3% of W jets, and zero for 73.7% of quark jets.
7.role: It raises the Z score (+35%), where it is the largest input, and the W score (+12%). It does not enter the g, q or t scores.

8.title: very narrow jets with a centred pT core (λ₁+λ₂ < 0.0036)
8.measures: Built from narrow-jet tests that partly cancel: λ₁+λ₂ < 0.00356 (+7.2%), ΣzΔR² < 0.00502 with pT share at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 below 0.101 (+6.2%), τ₁ < 0.0536 with λ₁+λ₂ < 0.00356 (+6.0%) and max ΔR(3 subjets) < 0.199 with ΣzΔR² < 0.00668 (+5.8%) push it up, while ΣzΔR < 0.0611 with ΣzΔR² < 0.00356 (-8.0%) and ΣzΔR < 0.0611 (-6.9%) push it down. It falls with the centroid offset (rank correlation -0.336) and λ₁+λ₂ (-0.32). Mean values: q (0.51), g (0.49), W (0.25), Z (0.11), t (0.07). It is zero for about half of the quark (51.1%) and gluon (54.0%) jets and for 87.1% of top jets.
8.role: It lowers the W score slightly (-2%). It does not enter the g, q, Z or t scores. Freezing it at its mean changes the accuracy by only -0.036 points.

9.title: narrow, centred jets (ΣzΔR² below 0.0061)
9.measures: Pushed up by ΣzΔR² < 0.0061 (+9.6%, its strongest term) and ΣzΔR² < 0.00356 (+7.1%), max ΔR(3 subjets) < 0.213 (+4.8%), centroid offset < 0.0184 (+4.5%) and total pT < 988 GeV (+4.5%).
